en.title: Hideo Kojima Declares New Resident Evil Movie a Masterclass in Gaming Adaptation
en.summary: The latest Resident Evil film is shattering box office records and has earned the ultimate seal of approval from gaming legend Hideo Kojima. He describes the movie not as a direct adaptation, but as an experience.
en.body:
The **Resident Evil** movie, directed by **Zach Cregger**, is proving to be a massive hit, not just with audiences but with some of the most discerning voices in the gaming world. It's currently on track to become the highest-grossing film in the franchise, even when adjusted for inflation, a testament to its broad appeal. While initially not on his radar, **Hideo Kojima**, the visionary behind titles like **Metal Gear Solid** and **Death Stranding**, recently caught the film and shared his enthusiastic take.

Kojima, known for his detailed social media commentary on media he genuinely enjoys, offered a glowing review. He highlighted the film's immediate impact, noting, "right from the opening, it hits you with music reminiscent of The Thing." He further elaborated that the movie delivers "a relentless barrage of classic horror techniques, terrifying situations, and jump scares that never lets up until the very end." This visceral approach seems to have resonated deeply with the acclaimed game designer.

## A New Benchmark for Adaptations

The most striking aspect of Kojima's praise is his perspective on what makes this **Resident Evil** film special. He articulated a sentiment echoed by many critics and fans: that the film transcends a typical story-for-screen adaptation. Instead, he believes it masterfully captures the essence of the player's journey.

> "This isn’t a film adaptation of ‘Resident Evil.’ It’s a film about the experience of playing Resident Evil with a controller in hand." — **Hideo Kojima**

This viewpoint aligns perfectly with the film's reported focus on translating the survival horror mechanics and the intense, often first-person, perspective that defines the beloved video game series. Critics have pointed to the use of POV shots and the emphasis on resource management and terrifying encounters as key elements that evoke the feeling of actually playing the game, rather than just watching a narrative unfold.

## The Fan Reaction and Franchise Future

For fans of **Resident Evil**, this endorsement from **Hideo Kojima** is significant. His ability to connect deeply with interactive media and translate those experiences into thoughtful commentary makes his praise a powerful indicator of the film's success in capturing the spirit of the games. The movie's impressive box office performance, coupled with such high-profile critical reception, suggests that **Zach Cregger** has found a formula that satisfies both long-time players and newcomers to the world of **Resident Evil**. This approach of adapting the *experience* rather than just the plot could set a new standard for how video game franchises are brought to the big screen.

## What's Next

With the **Resident Evil** film continuing its successful theatrical run and earning accolades, the future looks bright for this iteration of the franchise. Further details regarding potential sequels or related projects are expected to be announced as the film solidifies its box office standing.

So far it’s earned around $320 million in the global box office, but it has a few more weeks left in theaters to surpass Final Chapter ‘s inflation-adjusted $430 million. And the perk of its long theatrical run is that Kojima still had a chance to see it despite not being interested in checking it out at first. And he absolutely loved it, because if you know Kojima’s tendencies on social media, you’ll know he only writes paragraphs about the stuff he likes. Of Resident Evil , Kojima said that “right from the opening, it hits you with music reminiscent of The Thing . From there, it’s a relentless barrage of classic horror techniques, terrifying situations, and jump scares that never lets up until the very end.” He echoes some of our own sentiments, saying it’s more of an adaptation of the player rather than the game, which is exactly how we felt in our review . “This isn’t a film adaptation of “Resident Evil.” It’s a film about the experience of playing Resident Evil with a controller in hand,” he said. Kojima then reminisced on a time, 30 years ago, when he first tried the original Resident Evil game, saying the movie reminded him of his experience way back when. “I was just like Bryan in this movie. I kept getting game over after game over, shouting “F***!” over and over again. lol,” Kojima wrote. Hideo Kojima is a huge movie buff and, well, it sometimes feels like his games were meant to be live-action blockbusters rather than video games, despite their evident innovations. To see him loving a video game adaptation says a lot about Cregger’s achievement, and while it’s not the perfect movie by any means, it’s definitely up there with some of the greatest horror flicks of our generation. It’s brutal, it’s intense, fast-paced, and unrelenting, and that’s exactly how an RE film should feel. I just hope the next one includes just a little bit more of the source material, rather than just brushing it off.
